item.title: First case of New World screwworm found in U.S. wildlife, USDA says
item.description: The New World screwworm was detected in an elk that was discovered on a game ranch in Pecos County, Texas.

item.title: Video shows moments leading up to police fatally shooting toddler
item.description: The Mississippi attorney general announced the police officer will not be charged in connection with the killing of 1-year-old Kohen Wiley.

item.title: Why "dump dinners" are going viral for solving some of the mess of family dinners
item.description: Two Arizona parents found a creative way to avoid the dishes and complaints from their kids. Tony Dokoupil has the story.

item.title: How "Grey's Anatomy" helped a quick-thinking hero halt a runaway school bus
item.description: A quick-thinking hero helped save everyone aboard a runaway Minnesota school bus when the driver experienced a medical emergency. Jonah Kaplan has the story.

item.title: What to expect from El-Sayed vs. Rogers Senate debate in Michigan
item.description: Michigan Senate candidates Abdul El-Sayed and Mike Rogers are set to face off in their final debate before the midterms on Wednesday night. CBS News' Aaron Navarro has more details.

item.title: U.S. reducing troop footprint in Middle East, sources say
item.description: The U.S. military has been quietly reducing its footprint at posts in the Middle East due to ongoing regional threats from the Iran-backed Houthis and direct threats from Iran, sources tell CBS News.

item.title: Body cam video shows moments before Mississippi officer shot, killed one-year-old
item.description: Police body camera video posted by Darkhorse Press and verified by CBS News shows what happened moments before a Mississippi police officer shot and killed a one-year-old boy in pursuit of shoplifting suspects in a Walmart parking lot.

item.title: Former U.S. ambassador says Putin is a war criminal, calls Witkoff's comment "fatuous"
item.description: Former U.S. ambassador to Ukraine John Herbst joins "The Daily Report" to discuss Steve Witkoff's comment that Putin is a "humanitarian" following the release of an American citizen from a Russian prison.

item.title: Tennessee Titans cut defensive tackle Jordan Elliott after alleged gun incident
item.description: The head coach of the Tennessee Titans praised the character of defensive tackle Jordan Elliott after he was cut from the team on allegations he attempted to retrieve a gun after a fight during practice. Skyler Henry reports.

item.title: U.S. ordering some government staff to depart Saudi Arabia
item.description: The U.S. military has also been quietly reducing its footprint at posts in the Middle East due to regional threats from the Houthis and direct threats from Iran, CBS News has learned.

item.title: Surveillance video captures kidnapping attempt of 13-year-old girl in Florida
item.description: Surveillance video captured the moment a Florida man attempted to kidnap a young girl in a gas station parking lot before she broke free, authorities said. The 13-year-old can be seen walking home when a man in biking gear approaches her.

item.title: More details on report that Musk intentionally restricted Ukraine's access to SpaceX network
item.description: Elon Musk intentionally restricted Ukraine's access to a SpaceX satellite network crucial to its defense from Russia attacks, sources tell CBS News. Wall Street Journal national security reporter Alexander Ward joins "The Daily Report" to share more.

item.title: Retired NYPD detective charged in deadly road rage incident
item.description: A 46-year-old father was shot while sitting in rush hour traffic on the George Washington Bridge, which connects New York and New Jersey. A retired NYPD detective is in custody, sources said. Tom Hanson has more.

item.title: Ohio chemical facility leak prompts thousands to evacuate, creates potentially dangerous haze
item.description: A chemical storage facility in Toledo, Ohio, leaked chemicals over a wide residential area on Wednesday. Everyone within a one-mile radius was told to evacuate, and those within three miles were under orders to shut their windows and stay inside, pets included. Ash-har Quraishi has more information.

item.title: Vivek Ramaswamy under fire for attack ad featuring Amy Acton's mother
item.description: Ohio candidate for governor Vivek Ramaswamy is facing strong criticism for releasing an attack ad featuring his opponent Amy Acton's estranged mother. CBS News political director Fin Gómez has more.

item.title: Stephen Hubbard's son thanks Putin and Trump for father's release from Russian jail
item.description: Retired American teacher Stephen Hubbard has been released from a Russian jail after over four years of detention. His son, Joseph Coleman, spoke to CBS News about the good news. CBS News' Natalie Brand has more.

item.title: Son of detained American Stephen Hubbard reacts to Russia releasing him after 4 years
item.description: Russia released American Stephen Hubbard on Wednesday after four years of wrongfully detaining him. CBS News intelligence and national security reporter Olivia Gazis spoke with Hubbard's son about the release and joins to unpack their conversation. Then, CBS News chief White House correspondent Nancy Cordes reports on the Trump administration's response.

item.title: El-Sayed and Rogers facing off in 2nd Michigan Senate debate
item.description: Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers will meet on the debate stage in Michigan Wednesday night for the second and final time. CBS News White House and politics reporter Aaron Navarro has the latest.

item.title: Broad support for populist policies found across party lines in Wall Street Journal poll
item.description: Polarization exists between the two parties, but according to a survey conducted by The Wall Street Journal, many populist policies are finding broad support across party lines. Pollsters John Anzalone and Adam Geller, who conducted the survey, join "The Takeout" to break down their findings.

item.title: Political strategists on Ramaswamy attack ad against Amy Acton that features her estranged mother
item.description: Republican Vivek Ramaswamy's latest ad in the Ohio governor's race is drawing bipartisan pushback for featuring the estranged mother of his opponent, Democrat Amy Acton. Political strategists Mark Bednar and Santiago Mayer join "The Takeout" with analysis.

item.title: Pope Leo won't need more treatment after cancer surgery, doctors say
item.description: Pope Leo XIV will not need any further treatment after having lung cancer surgery, his doctors said in a statement.

item.title: Witkoff blasted for calling Putin a "humanitarian"
item.description: After special envoy Steve Witkoff told Putin he was a "humanitarian" for releasing a U.S. citizen deemed to have been wrongfully detained, GOP Sen. John Cornyn responded, "No. Putin is a stone cold killer."

item.title: 10/21: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: American Stephen Hubbard released by Russia after four years of wrongful detention; special envoy Steve Witkoff meets with Putin in Moscow.

item.title: Top DOJ official asks judges to step aside from immigration cases
item.description: A top official at the Justice Department is attempting to disqualify two Minnesota federal judges from a pair of cases related to immigration.

item.title: New Mexico AG accuses Epstein's lawyer, accountant of concealing crimes
item.description: New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez filed a lawsuit Wednesday against two of Jeffrey Epstein's closest confidants, attorney Darren Indyke and accountant Richard Kahn.

item.title: Meta ordered to pay $25 billion to New Mexico in data privacy ruling
item.description: A jury found that the social media company had deceived consumers for years about its data privacy policies.

item.title: Musk chose to restrict Ukraine's access to SpaceX network, sources say
item.description: A decision by Elon Musk led to restrictions on Ukraine's use of SpaceX's satellite communications network, people familiar with the matter told CBS News.

item.title: Armed federal agents knock on doors looking for noncitizen voters
item.description: Armed and in uniform, agents from the Department of Homeland Security have been knocking on doors to ask residents about their immigration status whether they're registered to vote.

item.title: Ohio race takes ugly turn with Ramaswamy ad featuring Acton's mom
item.description: Democrat Amy Acton's estranged mother calls her a liar in a new Ramaswamy campaign ad. Acton's brother says the ad marks a "despicable low" and says their stepfather sexually abused Acton when she was a child.

item.title: Trump spurs states to dump laws regulating new hospitals
item.description: The Trump administration has tied billions in rural health funding for states partly to the policy commitments they make, including ending their certificate of need, or CON, laws governing the construction of new hospitals.
